official_measurement_examples.name: Protected status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states otters and their breeding and resting places are protected by law.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning standing advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Otter standing advice is a material planning consideration when otters may be affected by development.

official_measurement_examples.name: A45 mitigation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A45 is required where development or other work would otherwise unlawfully affect otters.

official_measurement_examples.name: A45 decision period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states it will decide an A45 application within 30 working days after receiving the application.

official_measurement_examples.name: Reasoned statement
official_measurement_examples.fact: A45 applicants must provide evidence on licensing purpose and satisfactory alternatives through the required application evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: CL36 narrow scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL36 is limited to capture and transport of otters trapped in appropriately fenced fisheries to prevent serious damage.

official_measurement_examples.name: CL36 2026 validity
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current CL36 licence is valid from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030 subject to its conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Otter survey or licensing does not itself grant planning permission, prove otter absence or determine parcel development capacity.

core_rules: otter protection law is not proof otters are present on a parcel
otter survey result is not planning permission
planning permission is not an A45 otter mitigation licence
A45 mitigation licence is distinct from CL36 fishery class licence
CL36 is not a general development licence
planning standing advice is not a planning decision
reasoned statement is licence evidence not a planning grant
historic otter survey must retain its date and survey scope
absence of recorded holt is not proof of otter absence without adequate evidence
licence conditions must be tied to actual species activity and dates
otter protection does not determine land ownership
licensing does not reserve development capacity
CL36 landowner permission does not create ownership rights
otter compliance does not create access rights
no parcel otter clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
